narrative:
Your loan application was reviewed by our credit assessment system, which determined with an 81% likelihood that you represent a higher credit risk — a threshold that unfortunately led to the denial of your application. While several aspects of your profile are quite solid, three key factors drove this outcome, and understanding them may help you take steps toward a successful application in the future.

The single most influential factor in this decision was the current status of your checking account, which shows a negative balance. Among applicants who were approved, only about 1 in 5 had a negative checking account balance, while the majority either had no checking account or maintained a positive balance. A negative balance signals to the model that your day-to-day finances may already be under strain, which raises concerns about your ability to take on additional debt obligations.

The second major factor was your credit history, which is recorded as having no credits or all credits fully paid — a category that sounds positive on the surface but is actually quite rare among approved applicants, where fewer than 3% fell into this group. Counterintuitively, having no prior credit activity or a very clean slate can work against you, because it gives the model very little evidence of how you handle ongoing debt obligations over time. The vast majority of approved applicants had a track record of existing paid credits or even some past difficulties that were resolved, which provides a richer picture of creditworthiness.

The third contributing factor was the purpose of your loan — purchasing a new car. While this is a common reason for borrowing and nearly 20% of approved applicants also sought financing for a new car, it still carried some weight in pushing the prediction toward higher risk, likely in combination with the other two factors.

It is worth noting that several aspects of your profile are genuinely favorable: your requested amount of 1,082 DM is well below the average of nearly 2,887 DM among approved applicants, your loan duration of 12 months is shorter than the typical 19 months, and you own your home and have stable employment of 1 to 4 years. These factors did not outweigh the concerns raised above, but they are real strengths.

As a next step, we would encourage you to work on bringing your checking account into a positive balance before reapplying, as this was the strongest driver of the denial. If possible, establishing or demonstrating a clearer history of managing credit — such as a small credit line that you actively use and repay — could also significantly improve your profile. Speaking with a financial advisor or a bank representative about how to strengthen your application would be a worthwhile investment before your next attempt.
